name: VUV frequency comb for the Th-229 nuclear clock
summary: The 8.36 eV isomer of 229Th was excited with VUV lasers in 2024 and resolved with a VUV frequency comb made by cavity-enhanced seventh-harmonic generation of an infrared comb. The comb measured the transition's frequency ratio to the 87Sr optical clock and resolved its nuclear electric-quadrupole splitting in a CaF2 host. This makes a nuclear transition a candidate optical clock with enhanced sensitivity to variations of fundamental constants.

name: Cherenkov and transition-radiation detectors
summary: Cherenkov emission (cosθ_C = 1/nβ, Frank–Tamm photon yield) and transition radiation (yield ∝ γ) are the basis of threshold counters, ring-imaging Cherenkov detectors and TRDs. These identify electrons, pions and other hadrons in nuclear-physics spectrometers and the EIC's ePIC detector, and water-Cherenkov detectors use the same light to detect neutrinos. The Cherenkov angle gives β, which together with momentum gives the particle's mass.

name: Gamma-decay multipolarity is multipole radiation
summary: Nuclear γ transitions are classified as electric and magnetic 2^L-pole radiation and follow the selection rules of classical multipole radiation (EL parity (-1)^L, ML parity (-1)^(L+1)). Weisskopf single-particle estimates are the antenna formulas with nuclear transition moments inserted, and each extra multipole order costs a factor of about (kR)^2 ~ 10^-3–10^-5. That suppression is why high-L or very low-energy transitions give long-lived isomers such as the 8.4 eV M1 isomer of 229Th.

name: Bremsstrahlung, radiation length and showers
summary: Above the critical energy, electrons lose energy mainly by bremsstrahlung in nuclear Coulomb fields, the relativistic radiation of a decelerated charge. The radiation length X0 then sets how electromagnetic showers develop in calorimeters. Because the radiative-to-collisional loss ratio grows roughly as EZ, β shielding puts low-Z material first.

name: Synchrotron radiation and Sokolov–Ternov polarization
summary: Synchrotron power scales as γ^4/ρ^2; it limits the energy of electron storage rings and sets the EIC electron ring at up to 18 GeV. Spin-flip synchrotron emission self-polarizes stored electrons antiparallel to the field (Sokolov–Ternov, 92.4%), which HERA exploited. The EIC needs both helicities and self-polarization is slow, so it instead refreshes bunches from a polarized source while fighting radiative depolarization.
sources: Schwinger (1949). "On the Classical Radiation of Accelerated Electrons". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1912. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1912](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1912)

name: LPM suppression and QCD radiative energy loss
summary: When the formation time of a radiated quantum exceeds the mean free path, successive scatterings act coherently and suppress the radiation; for bremsstrahlung in dense matter this is the Landau–Pomeranchuk–Migdal effect. The BDMPS-Z and GLV radiative energy loss of quarks and gluons in the QGP is its non-Abelian version, governed by the transport coefficient q̂.
breaks: The radiated gluon carries colour and rescatters itself, which gives ΔE ∝ q̂L^2 rather than the QED scaling. The medium is also a rapidly expanding, strongly coupled plasma rather than a static solid.

name: Cyclotron radiation spectroscopy of tritium β electrons
summary: Project 8 measures β-electron energies from the frequency of their cyclotron radiation, f_c = eB/2πγm_e (~26 GHz near 1 T), picked up in a waveguide; the signal power is the Larmor power of a circulating charge. The goal is the neutrino mass from the tritium endpoint, and the experiment has already set a first tritium limit.

name: Laser Compton backscattering gamma sources
summary: Backscattering laser or FEL photons off relativistic electrons (inverse Compton scattering) produces tunable, quasi-monoenergetic, highly polarized MeV γ beams, as at HIγS. These beams are used to measure photonuclear cross sections and giant resonances, and for nuclear resonance fluorescence assays that identify specific isotopes.

name: Photon attenuation: photoelectric, Compton, pair
summary: Gamma-ray detection and shielding rest on the photon–matter cross sections of light-scattering theory: photoabsorption, Compton scattering with the Klein–Nishina cross section (which reduces to Thomson's σ_T at low energy), and pair production. Together these set the exponential attenuation coefficient μ(E,Z). The Compton edge and continuum seen in every γ spectrum follow directly from Compton kinematics.

name: Compton scattering off the nucleon: Thomson to DVCS
summary: Real Compton scattering off the nucleon has the low-energy structure of light scattering: a Thomson amplitude fixed by charge and mass, then a Rayleigh-like ω^2 term set by the electric and magnetic polarizabilities. The values α_E ≈ 11×10^-4 fm^3 and β_M ≈ 2.5×10^-4 fm^3 show the proton is a very stiff object. Deeply virtual Compton scattering is the same process in the Bjorken limit, where it accesses GPDs and the Ji spin sum rule.

name: Compton profiles and Bjorken scaling
summary: X-ray Compton profiles and Bjorken scaling in deep inelastic scattering are both impulse-approximation results. At large momentum transfer the probe scatters off quasi-free constituents, so the cross section depends on a single scaling variable and measures their momentum distribution: J(p_z) for electrons, q(x) for quarks. y-scaling in quasi-elastic electron–nucleus scattering is the intermediate case, for nucleons.
breaks: Partons are confined and relativistic, so the scaling variable is a light-cone momentum fraction and the final state hadronizes instead of escaping. QCD radiation also produces logarithmic scaling violations (DGLAP), which atomic Compton profiles do not have.
sources: Bjorken (1969). "Asymptotic Sum Rules at Infinite Momentum". *Phys. Rev.* 179, 1547. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.179.1547](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.179.1547)

name: Optical model as nuclear Mie scattering
summary: Elastic nucleon–nucleus scattering is described by a complex potential whose imaginary part absorbs flux into other channels. This is the quantum counterpart of Mie scattering by a sphere with a complex refractive index: both use partial-wave series, separate elastic from absorption cross sections and obey the optical theorem. The name 'optical model' (the 'cloudy crystal ball') comes directly from this analogy.
map: \nabla^2\psi+k^2n^2\psi=0\ \leftrightarrow\ n^2(\mathbf r)=1-\frac{U(\mathbf r)}{E},\ U=-(V+iW)f(r);\ \ \sigma_{\rm tot}=\frac{4\pi}{k}{\rm Im}f(0)
breaks: Mie theory is vectorial, with two coefficient series a_n and b_n for polarization, and uses a local, energy-independent index. The nuclear potential is scalar plus spin–orbit, energy-dependent and nonlocal, and the long-range Coulomb field distorts the partial waves of charged projectiles.
sources: Mie (1908). "Beiträge zur Optik trüber Medien, speziell kolloidaler Metallösungen". *Ann. Phys.* 330, 377. [doi:10.1002/andp.19083300302](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19083300302)

name: Reactors as heat sources for Rankine cycles
summary: Fission reactors and fusion plants are heat sources whose electrical efficiency (~33% for LWRs, more for high-temperature designs) is bounded by Carnot at the coolant outlet temperature and achieved with Rankine or Brayton cycles. Decay heat after shutdown is a thermodynamic safety problem.

name: Nuclear liquid–gas transition and the QCD phase diagram
summary: Strongly interacting matter has two first-order lines ending in Ising-class critical points: the nuclear liquid–gas transition (T_c≈15–18 MeV, near saturation density, from van der Waals-like nucleon interactions) and the conjectured chiral/deconfinement line at high μ_B. Multifragmentation caloric curves show a liquid–gas plateau, and coexistence follows the Gibbs conditions in (T, μ_B).
sources: Pochodzalla et al. (1995). "Probing the Nuclear Liquid-Gas Phase Transition". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 1040. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1040](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1040)
Du et al. (2025). "The QCD phase diagram and Beam Energy Scan physics: A theory overview". [arXiv:2402.10183](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10183)

name: Nuclear statistical equilibrium and the deuterium bottleneck
summary: Early-universe abundances follow the Saha/law-of-mass-action equation μ_A=Zμ_p+Nμ_n. Deuterium is suppressed until T≈0.07 MeV, well below its 2.2 MeV binding energy, because the photon-to-baryon ratio η⁻¹~10⁹ is huge (entropy wins).
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Gibbs vs Maxwell constructions and nuclear pasta
summary: With two conserved charges (baryon number and electric charge), a first-order hadron–quark or liquid–gas transition in a star can form a mixed phase under the Gibbs conditions instead of a sharp Maxwell interface. In the inner crust, Coulomb frustration of phase separation produces 'pasta' phases (rods, slabs).
sources: Glendenning (1992). "First-order phase transitions with more than one conserved charge: Consequences for neutron stars". *Phys. Rev. D* 46, 1274. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.46.1274](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.46.1274)
Ravenhall, Pethick & Wilson (1983). "Structure of Matter below Nuclear Saturation Density". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 50, 2066. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.2066](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.2066)

name: r-process waiting points as Saha equilibrium
summary: In the hot, neutron-rich r-process, (n,γ)⇌(γ,n) equilibrium along each isotopic chain is a Saha equation. Neutron density and temperature fix the waiting-point nuclei through their neutron separation energies, and β-decays then move material to higher Z.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: Liquid-drop model: nuclei as droplets of nuclear liquid
summary: The semi-empirical mass formula is the leptodermous (volume plus surface) expansion of a droplet of saturated, incompressible liquid. The volume term is the bulk chemical potential, and the surface term is a surface tension σ≈1 MeV/fm², the same capillarity that sets nucleation barriers.
map: B=a_VA-a_SA^{2/3}-\cdots\ \leftrightarrow\ G=-\Delta\mu N+4\pi r^2\sigma,\ a_S=4\pi r_0^2\sigma
breaks: Nuclei have only ~10–300 constituents, so curvature and shell corrections (magic numbers) are comparable to surface terms. The 'liquid' is a quantum Fermi liquid with pairing, not a classical van der Waals fluid.
sources: Weizsäcker (1935). "Zur Theorie der Kernmassen". *Z. Phys.* 96, 431. [doi:10.1007/BF01337700](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01337700)
Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)

name: Random-matrix theory born in compound nuclei
summary: Wigner introduced random matrices to model the dense resonances of compound nuclei. Level-spacing repulsion (Wigner surmise) and Porter–Thomas width distributions became, after Dyson's classification, a core tool of disordered and complex systems: mesoscopic transport, localization and spin glasses.
sources: Wigner (1955). "Characteristic Vectors of Bordered Matrices With Infinite Dimensions". *Ann. Math.* 62, 548. [doi:10.2307/1970079](https://doi.org/10.2307/1970079)

name: Colour-string percolation as a deconfinement model
summary: In string-percolation models, colour flux tubes from nucleon–nucleon collisions overlap as discs in the transverse plane. Deconfinement is identified with 2D continuum percolation of these discs at a critical density, which predicts the onset of collective effects with centrality.
breaks: Percolation is purely geometric and has no thermodynamics; the QCD transition at μ_B=0 is an analytic crossover with no diverging length. Connectivity of strings is not equivalent to deconfinement or thermalization.
sources: Satz (2000). "Colour deconfinement in nuclear collisions". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 63, 1511. [arXiv:hep-ph/0007069](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0007069)

name: Baryon-number cumulants as grand-canonical susceptibilities
summary: Lattice QCD and heavy-ion phenomenology use the grand-canonical relation between pressure derivatives and conserved-charge fluctuations: χ_n^B are cumulants of net baryon number. Real μ_B gives a complex Boltzmann weight (the sign problem), so lattice works by Taylor expansion or imaginary μ. Experiment must correct for global charge conservation, a canonical-ensemble effect.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)
Du et al. (2025). "The QCD phase diagram and Beam Energy Scan physics: A theory overview". [arXiv:2402.10183](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10183)

name: Statistical hadronization and the thermal model
summary: Hadron yields across species and collision energies follow a grand-canonical hadron-resonance-gas partition function with just T_ch≈156 MeV and μ_B(√s), which coincides with the lattice crossover. In small systems strangeness is suppressed because exact canonical conservation, not grand-canonical averaging, applies (ensemble inequivalence).
sources: Andronic et al. (2018). "Decoding the phase structure of QCD via particle production at high energy". *Nature* 561, 321. [arXiv:1710.09425](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.09425)

name: Compound-nucleus decay as microcanonical evaporation
summary: Bohr's compound nucleus 'forgets' how it formed and decays statistically. Weisskopf evaporation and Hauser–Feshbach theory compute decay widths from detailed balance and level densities, so emission spectra are Maxwellian with a nuclear temperature T=(∂ln ρ/∂E)^{-1}. This is microcanonical statistical mechanics of a ~100-body system.
sources: Weisskopf (1937). "Statistics and Nuclear Reactions". *Phys. Rev.* 52, 295. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.52.295](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.52.295)
Hauser & Feshbach (1952). "The Inelastic Scattering of Neutrons". *Phys. Rev.* 87, 366. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.87.366](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.87.366)

name: Parton entanglement entropy at small x
summary: Kharzeev and Levin proposed that the entanglement entropy between probed and unprobed regions of a proton at small x is S=ln(xG(x)), saturating the maximum for a dipole cascade. Hadron multiplicities measured in DIS are then compared with this entropy.
sources: Kharzeev & Levin (2017). "Deep inelastic scattering as a probe of entanglement". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 114008. [arXiv:1702.03489](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.03489)

name: Richardson's exact solution of the pairing model
summary: The reduced BCS pairing Hamiltonian for a finite set of levels is exactly solvable by Bethe-ansatz-type Richardson equations (Richardson–Gaudin integrability). It describes pairing in nuclei and ultrasmall superconducting grains beyond mean field, where BCS breaks down as Δ approaches the level spacing.
sources: Richardson (1963). "A restricted class of exact eigenstates of the pairing-force Hamiltonian". *Phys. Lett.* 3, 277. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(63)90259-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(63)90259-2)

name: Stefan–Boltzmann limit of the quark–gluon gas
summary: An ideal QGP is a relativistic Bose (gluons) plus Fermi (quarks) gas, ε/T⁴=(π²/30)(16+(21/2)n_f), and the jump in degrees of freedom across T_c signals deconfinement. Lattice EOS reaches only ~80% of this at a few T_c, a sign of strong coupling.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)

name: Neutron degeneracy pressure and β-equilibrium
summary: Neutron-star matter is a degenerate Fermi system. Oppenheimer and Volkoff found that an ideal neutron Fermi gas supports at most ~0.7 M_⊙, and the observed 2 M_⊙ stars require repulsive interactions. Equilibrium composition follows from μ_n=μ_p+μ_e at T≈0.
sources: Oppenheimer & Volkoff (1939). "On Massive Neutron Cores". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 374. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.374](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.374)

name: Fermi-gas nuclear level densities
summary: Bethe's level-density formula treats the nucleus as a degenerate Fermi gas. The Sommerfeld expansion gives E*=aT² and S=2aT, so ρ(E)∝exp(2√(aE)) with a≈A/8 MeV⁻¹. These level densities feed Hauser–Feshbach rates for reactors and the r-process.
sources: Bethe (1936). "An Attempt to Calculate the Number of Energy Levels of a Heavy Nucleus". *Phys. Rev.* 50, 332. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.50.332](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.50.332)

name: Chain reactions as critical branching processes
summary: A neutron chain reaction is a Galton–Watson branching process, and criticality k_eff=1 is its critical point, mean-field directed percolation (an absorbing-state transition with the zero population absorbing). Reactor-noise methods (Feynman-α, Rossi-α) use the diverging fluctuations near k=1 to measure subcriticality.
sources: Ryazanov (2026). "Multifractality, percolation threshold and critical point of a nuclear reactor". [arXiv:2601.03399](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03399)
Hinrichsen (2000). "Non-equilibrium critical phenomena and phase transitions into absorbing states". *Adv. Phys.* 49, 815. [arXiv:cond-mat/0001070](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0001070)

name: Gluon saturation as FKPP travelling fronts
summary: The Balitsky–Kovchegov equation for gluon saturation is in the universality class of the FKPP reaction–diffusion equation, so the saturation scale is the position of a pulled front in ln(1/x) and geometric scaling is front translation. Noise corrections (Brunet–Derrida) carry over from front-propagation statistics.
sources: Munier & Peschanski (2003). "Geometric scaling as traveling waves". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 91, 232001. [arXiv:hep-ph/0309177](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0309177)

name: Neutron transport is a linear Boltzmann equation
summary: Reactor physics solves the linear Boltzmann transport equation for neutron angular flux, with scattering, absorption and fission sources. Its P₁/diffusion approximation (Fick's law, diffusion length) and Fermi age theory of moderation are Chapman–Enskog-type reductions.

name: From kinetic theory to viscous relativistic hydrodynamics
summary: Second-order (Israel–Stewart) viscous hydrodynamics, the standard model of heavy-ion flow, is derived from the relativistic Boltzmann equation by Grad's moment method. Hadronic afterburners (UrQMD, SMASH) are Boltzmann transport, and the hydro-to-kinetic switch uses Cooper–Frye sampling of a local Jüttner distribution.
sources: Israel & Stewart (1979). "Transient relativistic thermodynamics and kinetic theory". *Ann. Phys.* 118, 341. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(79)90130-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(79)90130-1)

name: Neutron–proton freeze-out as rate competition
summary: The n/p ratio tracks its equilibrium value e^{-Q/T} until weak rates Γ∝G_F²T⁵ fall below the Hubble rate H∝T²/M_Pl at T_f≈0.8 MeV. That fixes Y_p≈0.25, a textbook example of kinetic freeze-out from a Boltzmann rate equation.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Gamow peak: Maxwell–Boltzmann tail times tunnelling
summary: Thermonuclear reaction rates are Maxwell–Boltzmann averages of the cross section. The falling exponential tail times the rising Gamow tunnelling factor gives a sharp peak at E₀ ≫ k_BT, so stellar burning and fusion-plasma reactivities ⟨σv⟩ sample only the far tail of the distribution.
sources: Bosch & Hale (1992). "Improved formulas for fusion cross-sections and thermal reactivities". *Nucl. Fusion* 32, 611. [doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07)

name: Kubo transport coefficients of the QGP
summary: QGP shear and bulk viscosities, conductivity and heavy-quark diffusion are defined by Kubo formulas. Lattice QCD obtains them from Euclidean correlators by inverting to spectral functions, an ill-posed analytic continuation, and flow data give η/s≈1–2 × ħ/4πk_B, near the holographic value.
sources: Kovtun, Son & Starinets (2005). "Viscosity in Strongly Interacting Quantum Field Theories from Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [arXiv:hep-th/0405231](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405231)

name: Giant resonances as nuclear linear response
summary: Giant dipole and monopole resonances are the nucleus's linear response to an external field. RPA is the time-dependent mean-field susceptibility, and energy-weighted sum rules (Thomas–Reiche–Kuhn) are f-sum rules fixed by commutators, as for conductivity or dielectric response.

name: Fano factor: sub-Poisson ionization statistics
summary: The number of ion pairs or electron–hole pairs created by a stopped particle fluctuates less than Poisson (Fano factor F≈0.1 in Ge), because total energy is fixed, as with microcanonical fluctuations. F sets the intrinsic energy resolution of gas and semiconductor detectors.
sources: Fano (1947). "Ionization Yield of Radiations. II. The Fluctuations of the Number of Ions". *Phys. Rev.* 72, 26. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.72.26](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.72.26)

name: Jet transverse-momentum broadening as diffusion
summary: A fast parton crossing the plasma takes random transverse kicks, so its transverse momentum random-walks: ⟨k_⊥²⟩=q̂L, with q̂ a momentum-diffusion coefficient. The coherent sum of induced radiation over this random walk gives the BDMPS ΔE∝q̂L² energy loss.
map: \langle k_\perp^2\rangle=\hat qL,\ \hat q=\rho\int d^2q_\perp q_\perp^2\frac{d\sigma}{d^2q_\perp};\ \Delta E\propto\alpha_s\hat qL^2
sources: Baier et al. (1997). "Radiative energy loss of high energy quarks and gluons in a finite-volume quark-gluon plasma". *Nucl. Phys. B* 483, 291. [arXiv:hep-ph/9607355](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9607355)

name: Heavy quarks as Brownian particles in the QGP
summary: Charm and bottom quarks (M≫T) diffuse through the plasma like Brownian particles. A Langevin equation with drag η_D and momentum-diffusion κ obeys the Einstein relation η_D=κ/2MT, and the spatial diffusion coefficient 2πTD_s is extracted from heavy-flavour R_AA and v₂.
sources: Moore & Teaney (2005). "How much do heavy quarks thermalize in a heavy ion collision?". *Phys. Rev. C* 71, 064904. [arXiv:hep-ph/0412346](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0412346)

name: Kramers escape theory was built for nuclear fission
summary: Kramers' 1940 theory of thermally activated escape over a barrier was motivated by Bohr–Wheeler fission and treated the fissioning nucleus as a Brownian particle in a viscous medium. Nuclear dissipation still appears as the Kramers factor that reduces fission rates and enhances pre-scission neutron emission.
sources: Kramers (1940). "Brownian motion in a field of force and the diffusion model of chemical reactions". *Physica* 7, 284. [doi:10.1016/S0031-8914(40)90098-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0031-8914(40)90098-2)
Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)

name: Radioactive decay as a Poisson process
summary: Decay is a memoryless Markov process: counts are Poisson, waiting times exponential, and decay chains obey Bateman's linear master equations. Counting statistics and dead-time corrections in nuclear detectors use the same stochastic-process tools.

name: Shape phase transitions in finite nuclei
summary: As nucleon number changes, nuclei go from spherical vibrators to deformed rotors through quantum shape phase transitions. Their Landau-theory description uses the quadrupole deformation as order parameter, and analytic critical-point symmetries such as X(5) and E(5) describe nuclei at the transition, which finite size rounds into crossovers.
sources: Iachello (2001). "Analytic Description of Critical Point Nuclei in a Spherical-Axially Deformed Shape Phase Transition". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 87, 052502. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.052502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.052502)

name: QCD critical point in the 3D Ising class
summary: A QCD critical endpoint, if it exists, lies in the 3D Ising (Z₂) universality class. (T, μ_B) map linearly onto Ising (t, h), and net-proton cumulant ratios scale with powers of ξ (κσ²∝ξ⁷), so beam-energy scans hunt for non-monotonic kurtosis. Finite-size scaling of cumulants is used to locate it.
sources: Stephanov (2009). "Non-Gaussian fluctuations near the QCD critical point". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 102, 032301. [arXiv:0809.3450](https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.3450)
Stephanov, Rajagopal & Shuryak (1998). "Signatures of the Tricritical Point in QCD". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 81, 4816. [arXiv:hep-ph/9806219](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9806219)
Sorensen & Sorensen (2024). "Locating the QCD critical point with finite-size scaling of proton cumulants". [arXiv:2405.10278](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.10278)

name: Relativistic mean-field theory of dense matter
summary: The Walecka σ–ω model replaces meson fields by their mean values, a Hartree mean-field theory in the spirit of Weiss. It reproduces nuclear saturation and gives a stiff neutron-star EOS, and Skyrme and RMF density functionals remain the main EOS inputs beyond ab initio densities.
sources: Walecka (1974). "A theory of highly condensed matter". *Ann. Phys.* 83, 491. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(74)90208-5](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(74)90208-5)

name: BCS pairing in nuclei
summary: Odd–even mass staggering, gaps in even–even spectra and reduced moments of inertia show that nucleons pair as in a superconductor. A BCS/Bogoliubov mean field with Δ≈12/√A MeV describes it, and the gap equation is the Landau–Ginzburg/BCS mean field of 03 applied to a finite Fermi system.
sources: Bohr, Mottelson & Pines (1958). "Possible Analogy between the Excitation Spectra of Nuclei and Those of the Superconducting Metallic State". *Phys. Rev.* 110, 936. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.110.936](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.110.936)

name: DGLAP evolution as a renormalization-group equation
summary: Q² dependence of parton distributions is the RG running of twist-2 operator matrix elements. Mellin moments scale with anomalous dimensions γ_n, exactly like scaling operators near a fixed point, and Bjorken scaling is the free-field fixed point of asymptotically free QCD.
sources: Altarelli & Parisi (1977). "Asymptotic freedom in parton language". *Nucl. Phys. B* 126, 298. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4)

name: SRG and V_low-k: Wilsonian RG for nuclear forces
summary: The similarity renormalization group (and IMSRG) is a continuous unitary RG flow that decouples high- and low-momentum states, the Wilsonian idea of integrating out short distances while keeping observables. It makes nuclear many-body calculations converge and generates induced three-body forces, the analogue of irrelevant couplings generated under RG.
sources: Bogner, Furnstahl & Schwenk (2010). "From low-momentum interactions to nuclear structure". *Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys.* 65, 94. [arXiv:0912.3688](https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.3688)

name: Efimov physics as an RG limit cycle
summary: Renormalizing the three-boson problem with contact interactions needs a three-body force whose coupling runs periodically in ln Λ: an RG limit cycle rather than a fixed point. This produces discrete scale invariance and the Efimov ratio 22.7, seen in cold atoms, light nuclei and halo systems.
sources: Bedaque, Hammer & van Kolck (1999). "Renormalization of the Three-Body System with Short-Range Interactions". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 82, 463. [arXiv:nucl-th/9809025](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/9809025)

name: Thorium-229 nuclear clock
summary: The 8.4 eV isomer of Th-229 has been laser-excited and frequency-referenced to a Sr clock, opening a nuclear optical clock highly sensitive to variations of alpha and the strong-interaction scale.
sources: Tiedau et al. (2024). "Laser Excitation of the Th-229 Nucleus". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 132, 182501. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.182501](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.182501)

Zhang et al. (2024). "Frequency ratio of the 229mTh nuclear isomeric transition and the 87Sr atomic clock". *Nature* 633, 63. [doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07839-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07839-6)

name: Proton radius from hydrogen and muonic hydrogen
summary: The finite proton size shifts S levels; muonic-hydrogen Lamb-shift spectroscopy gave r_p = 0.84 fm, 4% below earlier e-p values, and newer hydrogen spectroscopy largely agrees, resolving most of the proton-radius puzzle.
sources: Pohl et al. (2010). "The size of the proton". *Nature* 466, 213. [doi:10.1038/nature09250](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09250)
Bezginov et al. (2019). "A measurement of the atomic hydrogen Lamb shift and the proton charge radius". *Science* 365, 1007. [doi:10.1126/science.aau7807](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aau7807)

name: Multipole selection rules for atomic and nuclear photons
summary: Gamma transitions in nuclei obey the same multipole selection rules and Wigner-Eckart structure as atomic E1/M1/E2 lines; Weisskopf estimates and conversion electrons parallel atomic radiative and Auger channels.

name: Laser spectroscopy of exotic-nucleus radii and moments
summary: Isotope shifts and hyperfine structure measured by collinear laser spectroscopy give charge radii, spins and moments of short-lived nuclei, revealing halos and shell evolution far from stability.
sources: Garcia Ruiz et al. (2016). "Unexpectedly large charge radii of neutron-rich calcium isotopes". *Nature Phys.* 12, 594. [arXiv:1602.07906](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.07906)

name: Nuclear anapole moments from atomic parity violation
summary: The nuclear-spin-dependent part of Cs parity violation revealed the nuclear anapole moment, a probe of the parity-violating nucleon-nucleon (weak meson-exchange) interaction.
sources: Wood et al. (1997). "Measurement of Parity Nonconservation and an Anapole Moment in Cesium". *Science* 275, 1759. [doi:10.1126/science.275.5307.1759](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.275.5307.1759)

name: Laser spectroscopy of superheavy atoms
summary: Atom-at-a-time resonance ionization spectroscopy of nobelium measures level energies where relativistic effects reshape atomic structure, testing relativistic many-body theory and giving nuclear moments.
sources: Laatiaoui et al. (2016). "Atom-at-a-time laser resonance ionization spectroscopy of nobelium". *Nature* 538, 495. [doi:10.1038/nature19345](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature19345)

name: Elliptic flow of unitary gases and the QGP
summary: Strongly interacting Fermi gases released from anisotropic traps expand elliptically like the QGP's elliptic flow; both are nearly perfect fluids with eta/s near hbar/4 pi k_B.
breaks: Non-relativistic vs relativistic hydrodynamics; scales differ by ~1e19 in temperature; the QGP has gauge degrees of freedom and a crossover, the gas has none.
sources: O'Hara et al. (2002). "Observation of a Strongly Interacting Degenerate Fermi Gas of Atoms". *Science* 298, 2179. [arXiv:cond-mat/0212463](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0212463)
Schäfer & Teaney (2009). "Nearly perfect fluidity: from cold atomic gases to hot quark gluon plasmas". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 72, 126001. [arXiv:0904.3107](https://arxiv.org/abs/0904.3107)
Cao et al. (2011). "Universal Quantum Viscosity in a Unitary Fermi Gas". *Science* 331, 58. [arXiv:1007.2625](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.2625)

name: Cold-atom analogues of colour superfluidity
summary: Three-component Fermi gases with attractive interactions can form colour-superfluid and trion ('baryon') phases, an analogue of colour superconductivity and confinement in the dense QCD phase diagram.
breaks: No gauge field or gluon dynamics; trion formation is not confinement; densities map only qualitatively.

name: Unitary Fermi gas and dilute neutron matter
summary: The neutron-neutron scattering length (-18.5 fm) far exceeds the effective range, so low-density neutron matter is close to the unitary Fermi gas realized at Feshbach resonances; the measured Bertsch parameter benchmarks neutron-star crust EOS calculations.
sources: Carlson, Chang, Pandharipande & Schmidt (2003). "Superfluid Fermi Gases with Large Scattering Length". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 91, 050401. [arXiv:physics/0303094](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0303094)
Ku et al. (2012). "Revealing the Superfluid Lambda Transition in the Universal Thermodynamics of a Unitary Fermi Gas". *Science* 335, 563. [arXiv:1110.3309](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.3309)

name: Hoyle state as an alpha-particle condensate
summary: The 7.65 MeV Hoyle state of carbon-12 that enables triple-alpha burning has been described as a dilute gas of alpha clusters occupying one orbital, a nuclear analogue of a Bose condensate.
breaks: Only three or four bosons with Pauli effects among constituent nucleons; the condensate fraction is model dependent and debated.
sources: Tohsaki, Horiuchi, Schuck & Röpke (2001). "Alpha Cluster Condensation in 12C and 16O". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 87, 192501. [arXiv:nucl-th/0110014](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0110014)

name: Feshbach resonances: from nuclear reactions to cold atoms
summary: Feshbach developed closed-channel resonance theory for nuclear reactions; the same coupled-channel physics, tuned by magnetic field, became the main tool for controlling interactions in ultracold gases.
sources: Feshbach (1958). "Unified theory of nuclear reactions". *Ann. Phys.* 5, 357. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(58)90007-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(58)90007-1)
Chin et al. (2010). "Feshbach resonances in ultracold gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1225. [arXiv:0812.1496](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.1496)

name: BCS pairing in nuclei and Fermi gases
summary: Odd-even mass staggering and moments of inertia reflect BCS-like pairing in finite nuclei, the same gap equation as in BEC-BCS-crossover Fermi gases, with the cold-atom crossover a tunable laboratory for the regime. See the pairing-across-scales theme.
sources: Dean & Hjorth-Jensen (2003). "Pairing in nuclear systems: from neutron stars to finite nuclei". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 607. [arXiv:nucl-th/0210033](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0210033)

name: Scissors modes in deformed nuclei and BECs
summary: The scissors mode, a counter-rotation of proton and neutron clouds discovered in deformed nuclei, was predicted and observed in anisotropic BECs as a signature of superfluid irrotational flow.
breaks: In nuclei the mode is a proton-neutron relative rotation in a finite fermion system; in a BEC it is the tilt oscillation of a single bosonic superfluid.
sources: Guéry-Odelin & Stringari (1999). "Scissors Mode and Superfluidity of a Trapped Bose-Einstein Condensed Gas". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 83, 4452. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.4452](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.4452)

Maragò et al. (2000). "Observation of the Scissors Mode and Evidence for Superfluidity of a Trapped Bose-Einstein Condensed Gas". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 84, 2056. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.84.2056](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.84.2056)

name: Laser-trapped radioactive atoms for weak-interaction tests
summary: Magneto-optical and dipole traps hold short-lived radioactive atoms nearly at rest, so recoiling nuclei and beta-neutrino angular correlations can be measured cleanly to search for scalar and tensor weak currents.

name: Quarkonium in the QGP as an open quantum system
summary: Heavy quark-antiquark pairs coupled to the QGP bath obey Lindblad equations derived from pNRQCD, describing screening, dissociation and regeneration of quarkonia beyond rate equations.
sources: Brambilla, Escobedo, Soto & Vairo (2017). "Quarkonium suppression in heavy-ion collisions: an open quantum system approach". *Phys. Rev. D* 96, 034021. [arXiv:1612.07248](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.07248)

name: Random-matrix theory began with nuclear resonances
summary: Wigner and Dyson introduced random matrices to model neutron-resonance spacings in heavy nuclei; the nuclear data ensemble later anchored the Bohigas-Giannoni-Schmit link between classical chaos and Wigner-Dyson statistics.
sources: Wigner (1955). "Characteristic Vectors of Bordered Matrices With Infinite Dimensions". *Ann. Math.* 62, 548. [doi:10.2307/1970079](https://doi.org/10.2307/1970079)
Dyson (1962). "Statistical Theory of the Energy Levels of Complex Systems. I". *J. Math. Phys.* 3, 140. [doi:10.1063/1.1703773](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1703773)

Bohigas, Giannoni & Schmit (1984). "Characterization of Chaotic Quantum Spectra and Universality of Level Fluctuation Laws". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 52, 1. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1)

name: Thermalization of an isolated QCD system
summary: Heavy-ion collisions pose the isolated-system thermalization problem at strong coupling: how a far-from-equilibrium gluon state reaches hydrodynamic behaviour in ~1 fm/c, with links to prethermalization and non-thermal fixed points studied in cold atoms.
sources: Berges, Heller, Mazeliauskas & Venugopalan (2021). "QCD thermalization: Ab initio approaches and interdisciplinary connections". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 93, 035003. [arXiv:2005.12299](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.12299)

name: Compound nucleus as a thermalizing system
summary: Bohr's compound nucleus forgets how it was formed and decays statistically, an early instance of an isolated many-body quantum system thermalizing; Hauser-Feshbach and evaporation theory use nuclear temperature.
sources: Bohr (1936). "Neutron Capture and Nuclear Constitution". *Nature* 137, 344. [doi:10.1038/137344a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/137344a0)

name: Entanglement entropy in deep inelastic scattering
summary: The parton distribution probed at small x has been interpreted as the entanglement entropy between the probed region and the rest of the proton, linking DIS multiplicities to quantum information.
sources: Kharzeev & Levin (2017). "Deep inelastic scattering as a probe of entanglement". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 114008. [arXiv:1702.03489](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.03489)

name: Quantum computing of nuclear ground states
summary: Variational quantum eigensolvers computed the deuteron binding energy from pionless/chiral EFT Hamiltonians on cloud processors, a first step toward quantum simulation of nuclear many-body problems.
sources: Dumitrescu et al. (2018). "Cloud Quantum Computing of an Atomic Nucleus". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 120, 210501. [arXiv:1801.03897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.03897)

name: Odd-even pairing effects in nuclei and SC islands
summary: Small superconducting islands show an even-odd ground-state energy difference from an unpaired quasiparticle, the same blocking effect behind nuclear odd-even mass staggering; quasiparticle poisoning of charge qubits is its device consequence.
map: \Delta E_{\rm odd-even}\approx\Delta\ (\text{gap});\ E_{\rm odd}-E_{\rm even}=\Delta-k_BT\ln N_{\rm eff}

name: Penning-trap mass spectrometry
summary: Ion-trap techniques measure masses of exotic nuclei to 1e-8 or better via cyclotron frequencies, fixing separation energies, shell gaps and drip lines.
sources: Blaum (2006). "High-accuracy mass spectrometry with stored ions". *Phys. Rep.* 425, 1. [doi:10.1016/j.physrep.2005.10.011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physrep.2005.10.011)

name: Spin-orbit coupling and magic numbers
summary: A strong nuclear spin-orbit term splits j=l+-1/2 levels and reproduces the magic numbers; jj-coupling, Clebsch-Gordan and Wigner-Eckart machinery from atomic physics then organizes shell-model states.
breaks: Same operator algebra but different physics: nuclear spin-orbit is a strong-interaction effect, ~20x larger relative to level spacing, with inverted ordering relative to atomic fine structure.
sources: Mayer (1949). "On Closed Shells in Nuclei. II". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1969. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969)

name: WKB tunnelling and the Gamow peak
summary: Thermonuclear fusion proceeds by WKB tunnelling through the Coulomb barrier; the product of Maxwell-Boltzmann tail and penetrability gives the Gamow peak that sets stellar and fusion-reactor rates.

name: Alpha decay as Coulomb-barrier tunnelling
summary: Gamow and Gurney-Condon explained alpha decay as tunnelling through the Coulomb barrier; the barrier-penetration factor gives the Geiger-Nuttall law spanning 20+ orders of magnitude in half-life.
sources: Gamow (1928). "Zur Quantentheorie des Atomkernes". *Z. Phys.* 51, 204. [doi:10.1007/BF01343196](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01343196)
Gurney & Condon (1928). "Wave Mechanics and Radioactive Disintegration". *Nature* 122, 439. [doi:10.1038/122439a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/122439a0)

name: Least-action paths for spontaneous fission
summary: Spontaneous-fission lifetimes are computed as imaginary-time tunnelling along least-action paths in a multidimensional collective space, an instanton/WKB calculation with a coordinate-dependent inertia.
sources: Schunck & Robledo (2016). "Microscopic theory of nuclear fission: a review". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 79, 116301. [arXiv:1511.07517](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.07517)

name: Coulomb wavefunctions and the Gamow factor
summary: Charged-particle reaction rates factor into a smooth astrophysical S-factor and the Sommerfeld/Gamow penetrability that comes from exact Coulomb scattering wavefunctions at the origin.

name: Partial waves, resonances and the optical model
summary: Nuclear reaction theory is applied quantum scattering theory: phase shifts and partial waves, Breit-Wigner compound resonances, the complex optical potential (absorption via Im V), and R-matrix fits of cross sections.

name: Large scattering length: pionless EFT and cold atoms
summary: Pionless EFT for nucleons and the effective theory of Feshbach-tuned atoms share universal large-scattering-length physics: shallow dimers (deuteron), the three-body parameter and Efimov-like states in nuclei and halos.
sources: Braaten & Hammer (2006). "Universality in few-body systems with large scattering length". *Phys. Rep.* 428, 259. [arXiv:cond-mat/0410417](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0410417)

name: Photon-counting detectors shared with radiation detection
summary: Scintillation and gamma spectroscopy rely on single-photon-sensitive photodetectors (PMTs, SiPMs), while transition-edge-sensor microcalorimeters developed for quantum optics give eV resolution for gamma and X-ray lines.

name: Hawking-Page transition as deconfinement
summary: In AdS, thermal gas and large black holes exchange dominance at the Hawking-Page temperature; holographically this is the confinement-deconfinement transition of the boundary gauge theory, with free energy jumping from O(N^0) to O(N^2).
breaks: Holographic transition is first-order at large N; QCD with physical quarks is a crossover at mu_B=0.
sources: Hawking & Page (1983). "Thermodynamics of Black Holes in anti-De Sitter Space". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 87, 577. [doi:10.1007/BF01208266](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01208266)
Witten (1998). "Anti-de Sitter space, thermal phase transition, and confinement in gauge theories". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 505. [arXiv:hep-th/9803131](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9803131)

name: Gravitational form factors and proton pressure
summary: Matrix elements of the QCD energy-momentum tensor, the source of gravity, define the proton's gravitational form factors A, B, D; Ji's sum rule gives quark angular momentum and the D-term gives the internal pressure, extracted from deeply virtual Compton scattering.
breaks: Direct graviton scattering is unmeasurable; extraction relies on GPD models and dispersion relations, so the pressure profile is model dependent.
sources: Burkert, Elouadrhiri & Girod (2018). "The pressure distribution inside the proton". *Nature* 557, 396. [doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0060-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0060-z)

Polyakov & Schweitzer (2018). "Forces inside hadrons: pressure, surface tension, mechanical radius, and all that". *Int. J. Mod. Phys. A* 33, 1830025. [arXiv:1805.06596](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.06596)

name: Israel-Stewart causal hydrodynamics
summary: First-order (Navier-Stokes) relativistic viscous hydrodynamics is acausal and unstable; Israel and Stewart's second-order theory, built for relativistic fluids in GR, relaxes the shear tensor over a time tau_pi and underlies modern heavy-ion hydrodynamics.
sources: Israel & Stewart (1979). "Transient relativistic thermodynamics and kinetic theory". *Ann. Phys.* 118, 341. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(79)90130-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(79)90130-1)

name: TOV equation: GR hydrostatics of nuclear matter
summary: The Einstein equations for a static perfect-fluid sphere give the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equation; each nuclear EOS P(epsilon) maps to a unique mass-radius curve and maximum mass, so 2 M_sun pulsars rule out soft EOSs.
sources: Oppenheimer & Volkoff (1939). "On Massive Neutron Cores". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 374. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.374](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.374)
Tolman (1939). "Static Solutions of Einstein's Field Equations for Spheres of Fluid". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 364. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.364](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.364)

name: BBN constrains G and extra gravitational fields
summary: The neutron-proton freeze-out temperature depends on the expansion rate H proportional to sqrt(G rho); primordial helium and deuterium bound any change of G between BBN and today to roughly 10-20% and limit scalar-tensor and extra-radiation models.
sources: Copi, Davis & Krauss (2004). "A new nucleosynthesis constraint on the variation of G". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 92, 171301. [arXiv:astro-ph/0311334](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0311334)

name: Mergers probe a hadron-quark phase transition
summary: Neutron-star merger remnants reach several times saturation density at T of tens of MeV, a region of the QCD phase diagram heavy-ion collisions cannot reach; a strong first-order transition shifts the post-merger GW frequency away from the hadronic f2-radius relation.
breaks: Post-merger signals at kHz are below current sensitivity; the signature requires third-generation detectors.
sources: Most et al. (2019). "Signatures of quark-hadron phase transitions in general-relativistic neutron-star mergers". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 122, 061101. [arXiv:1807.03684](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03684)

Bauswein et al. (2019). "Identifying a first-order phase transition in neutron star mergers through gravitational waves". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 122, 061102. [arXiv:1809.01116](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.01116)

name: Merger simulations with nuclear EOS
summary: GR hydrodynamic simulations of binary neutron-star mergers with tabulated finite-temperature nuclear EOSs predict prompt-collapse thresholds, remnant lifetimes and the post-merger f2 frequency, which correlates with stellar radius.
map: f_2\approx\text{few kHz},\quad f_2\propto\sqrt{M/R^3};\quad M_{\rm thr}\approx k\,M_{\rm max}^{\rm TOV},\ k\sim1.3\text{--}1.7
sources: Shibata et al. (2017). "Modeling GW170817 based on numerical relativity and its implications". *Phys. Rev. D* 96, 123012. [arXiv:1710.07579](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.07579)

name: Merger ejecta and electron fraction from NR
summary: Which nuclei a merger makes depends on the ejecta electron fraction Y_e, set by shock heating and neutrino irradiation in NR simulations with neutrino transport; dynamical ejecta (Y_e < 0.25) make the third r-process peak, disk winds lighter elements.
breaks: Nucleosynthesis yields are sensitive to neutrino transport approximations and to unmeasured masses of very neutron-rich nuclei.
sources: Shibata et al. (2017). "Modeling GW170817 based on numerical relativity and its implications". *Phys. Rev. D* 96, 123012. [arXiv:1710.07579](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.07579)

name: Mossbauer gamma lines measured gravitational redshift
summary: Pound and Rebka resolved a fractional shift of 2.5e-15 over 22.5 m by using the recoil-free 14.4 keV nuclear gamma transition of Fe-57, whose natural linewidth made the nuclear transition a clock fine enough to see gravity.
sources: Pound & Rebka (1960). "Apparent Weight of Photons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 4, 337. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337)

name: Equivalence-principle tests weigh nuclear binding
summary: Eotvos-type and MICROSCOPE tests compare materials whose mass-energy differs in nuclear binding and Coulomb energy fractions; a violating dilaton couples to these 'charges', so nuclear structure (B/A, Z(Z-1)/A^{4/3}) sets what an EP test probes.
sources: Damour (2012). "Theoretical aspects of the equivalence principle". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 29, 184001. [arXiv:1202.6311](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.6311)

name: Love numbers enter the 5PN waveform phase
summary: The quadrupole induced by the companion's tidal field, Q = -lambda E, adds a term scaling as Lambda (v/c)^10 to the inspiral phase; computing k_2 needs a perturbed TOV solution, so EOS physics enters waveform models directly.
sources: Flanagan & Hinderer (2008). "Constraining neutron star tidal Love numbers with gravitational wave detectors". *Phys. Rev. D* 77, 021502. [arXiv:0709.1915](https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1915)
Hinderer (2008). "Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars". *Astrophys. J.* 677, 1216. [arXiv:0711.2420](https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.2420)

name: Tidal deformability from GW170817
summary: Tidal deformation of inspiralling neutron stars shifts the GW phase; GW170817 bounded the combined tidal deformability and hence radii near 11-13 km, excluding the stiffest nuclear equations of state.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2018). "GW170817: Measurements of neutron star radii and equation of state". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 161101. [arXiv:1805.11581](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11581)

name: GW170817 kilonova as an r-process site
summary: The GW-localized merger GW170817 produced a kilonova whose red, lanthanide-rich emission powered by r-process decay showed that neutron-star mergers make heavy elements, tying nuclear masses and beta rates to GW sources.
map: L(t)\propto M_{\rm ej}\,\dot\epsilon(t),\ \dot\epsilon\propto t^{-1.3};\quad M_{\rm ej}\sim0.05\,M_\odot
sources: Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [arXiv:1710.05463](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05463)

name: BBN bound on primordial GW backgrounds
summary: Any primordial GW background present before BBN is extra radiation and raises N_eff; the light-element abundances cap its integrated energy density, a benchmark that LISA and PTA cosmological interpretations must respect.
sources: Caprini & Figueroa (2018). "Cosmological backgrounds of gravitational waves". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 35, 163001. [arXiv:1801.04268](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04268)

name: Holographic thermalization of heavy-ion collisions
summary: Colliding gravitational shock waves in AdS5 form a black brane within about 1/T, modelling rapid hydrodynamization of the fireball; horizon formation plays the role of thermalization.
breaks: Infinite-coupling, infinite-N model; real collisions have weak-coupling early stages (glasma) and finite N.
sources: Chesler & Yaffe (2011). "Holography and colliding gravitational shock waves in asymptotically AdS5 spacetime". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 106, 021601. [arXiv:1011.3562](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.3562)

name: Fluid/gravity correspondence
summary: Slowly varying black branes in AdS5 are dual to solutions of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics; the bulk Einstein equations order by order in gradients yield the transport coefficients of second-order hydrodynamics used in heavy-ion codes.
sources: Bhattacharyya et al. (2008). "Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics from Gravity". *JHEP* 02, 045. [arXiv:0712.2456](https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.2456)

name: Trailing strings and holographic jet quenching
summary: A heavy quark crossing a strongly coupled plasma is a string trailing into a black-brane horizon; the drag force and jet quenching parameter q-hat follow in closed form, giving estimates comparable to RHIC/LHC energy-loss data.
breaks: N=4 SYM rather than QCD, and the perturbative early-time regime of jets is missing.
sources: Gubser (2006). "Drag force in AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. D* 74, 126005. [arXiv:hep-th/0605182](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0605182)
Liu, Rajagopal & Wiedemann (2006). "Calculating the jet quenching parameter from AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 97, 182301. [arXiv:hep-ph/0605178](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0605178)

name: eta/s = 1/4pi from black-brane horizons
summary: Shear viscosity of a strongly coupled plasma equals the absorption of gravitons by a black-brane horizon; for every two-derivative gravity dual eta/s = hbar/4pi k_B, close to the small eta/s extracted from RHIC/LHC flow.
breaks: N=4 SYM is conformal, supersymmetric and large-N; QCD near T_c is none of these, and the 1/4pi value is violated by higher-curvature corrections.
sources: Kovtun, Son & Starinets (2005). "Viscosity in strongly interacting quantum field theories from black hole physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [arXiv:hep-th/0405231](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405231)

name: Hadronization as Unruh radiation
summary: Thermal hadron yields with a universal T near 160 MeV in e+e-, pp and AA have been modelled as Unruh radiation from quarks decelerated by the string tension at a confinement horizon, with T = a/2pi and a ~ sqrt(sigma).
breaks: The confinement 'horizon' is not a spacetime horizon; universal thermal yields also follow from statistical hadronization without any Unruh mechanism.
sources: Castorina, Kharzeev & Satz (2007). "Thermal hadronization and Hawking-Unruh radiation in QCD". *Eur. Phys. J. C* 52, 187. [arXiv:0704.1426](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.1426)

name: Rapidity and Bjorken boost-invariant flow
summary: Lorentz boosts along the beam add rapidities, so a boost-invariant expansion depends only on proper time tau; Bjorken's solution of relativistic hydrodynamics gives the initial energy-density estimate used in every heavy-ion analysis.
sources: Bjorken (1983). "Highly relativistic nucleus-nucleus collisions: The central rapidity region". *Phys. Rev. D* 27, 140. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.27.140](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.27.140)

name: Q-values and the direct test of E=mc^2
summary: Nuclear reaction energetics are mass-energy equivalence in action: Q = (sum m_i - sum m_f)c^2; comparing neutron-capture gamma energies with Penning-trap mass differences verified E=mc^2 to 4e-7.
sources: Rainville et al. (2005). "A direct test of E=mc^2". *Nature* 438, 1096. [doi:10.1038/4381096a](https://doi.org/10.1038/4381096a)

name: Hughes-Drever tests with nuclear spins
summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance of nuclei with J > 1/2 (Li-7, and modern He-3/Xe-129 comagnetometers) searches for quadrupole splitting varying with sidereal orientation; shell-model wavefunctions convert the bounds into limits on proton and neutron SME coefficients near 1e-30 GeV.
breaks: Interpreting a bound requires a nuclear model of which nucleons carry the spin, adding model dependence.
sources: Hughes, Robinson & Beltran-Lopez (1960). "Upper Limit for the Anisotropy of Inertial Mass from Nuclear Resonance Experiments". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 4, 342. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.342](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.342)
